caption: The drawing is on a decorative round plate with a scalloped edge, rendered in black and white. Around the border of the plate are the names of the original thirteen American colonies—such as Massachusetts, New York, Delaware, and Virginia—each separated by star motifs. The central image within an ornate frame depicts a large building with several windows, surrounded by trees, grazing sheep, and several small human figures. On the left edge of the central image stands a man labeled “Washington,” next to a female figure holding a pole and banner. Beneath them is a ribbon with the text “AMERICA AND.” On the right, another female figure in classical attire, wearing a helmet and holding a shield and spear, is seated beside another ribbon labeled “INDEPENDENCE.” Decorative floral arrangements, including large blossoms and fruit with leaves, fill the areas above and below the central scene. The composition integrates ornamental motifs, human figures, text ribbons, and symbolic references, all in a monochrome tonal scheme.
title: Plate - University Building
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
